audit.note: R87's additive null had CV R2 -0.034; this one includes per-drug log-dose slopes

limits: Each drug has only a few concentration points, so the slope estimates are unstable.
Residuals may still be dominated by well-level noise.
Retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim; no meta-learning or RSI.

correction_to_R87.R87_claim: the additivity residual is noise (CV R2 = -0.034), so BATCHIE cannot test the question
correction_to_R87.what_was_actually_wrong: R87 averaged every (pair, dose) well into one value per pair, discarding the dose structure; the negative R2 measured a weak null model, not an unlearnable residual
correction_to_R87.R88_evidence: adding per-drug log-dose slopes raises the null's CV R2 from -0.034 to +0.651
correction_to_R87.consequence: BATCHIE CAN discriminate; R87's 'resource unusable' verdict was wrong on the residual arm

honest_reading_of_the_comparison: with the gate now passed, the annotation model scores 29.06% against random 26.25%, a point estimate of +2.81 pp whose CI [-5.42, +11.88] includes zero. So the correct statement is 'no established gain', not 'the model loses' - the pre-registered H226 criterion only licensed 'not significantly better', and with 48 units the test is underpowered.
